data.description:
Board request (human:forrest, DM conversation 7, msg 521, 2026-09-03): "we need issues to set up posthog and sentry low priority but observability needs to be on the radar". This is the design task; the three instrumentation tasks (Sentry on apps/invoicing, PostHog on apps/invoicing, Sentry on apps/chat + watcher) depend on it and must not start until it is done.

WHY A DESIGN TASK FIRST, NOT STRAIGHT TO INSTRUMENTATION. Three things make this a decision rather than plumbing:

1. The stack decision (docs/engineering/01-stack-decision.md §11) already rules on this. Rule 3: any dependency that requires a hosted service, an API key, or registration of any kind is a board ask, no threshold. Rule 5: the suite must still run under --network none. Rule 4: transitive footprint is counted (the Sentry Node SDK carries an OpenTelemetry tree; PostHog's node SDK is smaller but not zero). And apps/invoicing/test/dependency-policy.test.js line 557 asserts that no app source outside the Stripe client module contains an outbound HTTP client — a Sentry/PostHog SDK dropped into the app fails that guard by construction. The design has to say how a second (and third) egress channel coexists with the chokepoint rule: the default answer to evaluate is one egress module per external service, each with its own chokepoint test, mirroring lib/stripe.

2. Data handling. apps/invoicing holds freelancer credentials, client names and emails, contract text, and invoice mirrors (amounts, line items, Stripe ids). An error-tracking payload that captures request bodies or local variables, or an analytics event that carries invoice contents, moves that data to a third party. "Never in the flow of funds" is a custody constraint on money, but the same instinct applies here: an analytics pipeline that mirrors invoice contents is a data-handling decision, not a plumbing one. The design must produce an explicit allow-list of what leaves the machine (event names, hashed/opaque ids, error type + stack, app version) and a deny-list (PII, amounts, line items, contract text, session tokens, Stripe ids), and say how the deny-list is enforced by a test, not by review discipline. Sentry's beforeSend / PostHog's property sanitisation are where this lands if SDKs are used; a hand-rolled egress module makes it a schema.

3. Self-hosted vs cloud changes what the board ask IS. Cloud Sentry / cloud PostHog: an account (free tier), a DSN/API key, and product data resident with a vendor under their DPA. Self-hosted: no vendor DPA question, but a Digital Ocean droplet (spend) and an ops surface we own — PostHog self-hosted in particular is a multi-service deployment. Either path is board-gated (see below); the design decides which one to ask for and why.

SCOPE OF THE DELIVERABLE: a written design note at docs/engineering/04-observability-posture.md covering (a) what is instrumented on which surface and why the two apps differ (invoicing is the product with real users; chat is internal tooling whose only users are employees and the board — product analytics there is meaningless, error tracking has modest value mainly for the headless watcher whose failures have historically been silent, see AS-21); (b) SDK vs raw ingest API — both Sentry (envelope endpoint) and PostHog (/capture, /batch) accept plain HTTP, so a zero-new-dependency egress module using node fetch is a live option that sidesteps rules 4 and 5 entirely; the note measures the transitive footprint of the SDK route per rule 4 before choosing; (c) the data allow/deny-list above and its enforcing test; (d) self-hosted vs cloud with the cost/ops tradeoff stated; (e) the exact board ask, written as one scannable needs_human comment, ready to file. Time-box: one planning-stage session; default answer if the box expires: raw ingest via a fetch-based egress module, cloud free tier, deny-list enforced by a schema test, ask filed for both vendors at once.

BOARD GATE (non-negotiable, from CLAUDE.md product section): every external service signup is board-gated, including free and test-mode accounts. This task creates NO accounts, requests NO keys, sends NO data anywhere. It PRODUCES the ask; the ask is filed as a separate needs_human item when this task closes. Rationale for deferring the ask rather than filing it now: AS-51 (Stripe test-mode account) is already parked on the board's desk, and the observability ask cannot be written honestly until self-hosted vs cloud is decided — a cloud ask is "approve two free accounts", a self-hosted ask is "approve a droplet". Asking before knowing which would be asking the board to do the design.

PRIORITY: low, per the board's own words. Does not jump the D1 line (AS-45/46/47/48/49/50/70) or the chat cluster (AS-27, AS-75, AS-28, AS-73, AS-74, AS-72, AS-61). Sequencing recommendation: pick this up when an implementer lane is idle; the Sentry-on-invoicing task should land before the first non-employee user touches the product (an error we cannot see is one we cannot fix), PostHog-on-invoicing after there are users to measure.
data.title: Observability: design note — error tracking + product analytics posture for apps/invoicing and apps/chat (Sentry/PostHog; produces the board ask)

data.body:
Design note written and committed to feat/AS-76-observability-design (086f0c4): docs/engineering/04-observability-posture.md, ~460 lines, sections (a)-(e) all covered. Not transitioned — orchestrator's call.

RULINGS. (a) invoicing gets both instruments, server-side only; browser-side declined in v1. chat gets neither: analytics over 11 internal identities is noise, and all three silent-failure incidents on the record (AS-21, the 605s lane terminations, watcher:57637) were NON-EVENTS, which error tracking cannot detect by construction. Recommends re-scoping AS-79 to watcher/chat fault events into the existing company event stream + an absence projection (zero deps, zero egress, zero signup, internal-tools lane, so NOT blocked on the board), with a reopening trigger if either moves off the board member's machine. Board gets an explicit one-line override in the ask rather than a silent narrowing. (b) Raw HTTP ingest for both, not SDKs. (c) Additive allow-list, 3 tests + 6 falsifiers; error MESSAGE denied. (d) Cloud free tier + a hard local daily cap. (e) Ask drafted verbatim, ready to paste, with filing notes.

EVIDENCE (all reproducible offline, receipts + README under scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-76/): @sentry/node@10.68.0 closure >=33 distinct packages, 67 -> 100 (+49%) against a 2-direct budget, and it contains meriyah + astring + import-in-the-middle, i.e. a load-time source rewriter — the decisive argument, since our custody guard is a lexical scan of committed source. posthog-node is 3 packages, all MIT, no loader hooks: the closest call, with its flip condition stated. Licences: 0 non-permissive either side; no install scripts either side. Message ruling: 185 throw sites, 60 interpolate a runtime value, 10 a deny-listed one, 2 a Stripe object id at named lines.

CAVEAT: no network this session, so rule 4's npm ls could not run. Substitute closure walk validates itself by re-deriving the app's recorded 69/67 footprint and licence spread exactly; all its limits err low, so counts are stated as a floor. Recorded as a method divergence in the note's amendment log. Carried as Q5.

Also carried: Q6, the 04- filename collision with 04-glossary.md — left as specified because three tasks' criteria name the path.

VERDICT: implementation-level rework needed. Read plan and diff cold; read the implementer's comment LAST, after findings were formed. Reproductions: scratchpad/agent-qa-ruben/AS-76/battery-log.md

Every measured number in the note reproduces exactly (footprint 32/3/35, 67->100 +49%; throw sites 185/60/10; licence spreads; zero install scripts; node-core's 5 peerDeps; corollary 3's bare `return value`). The evidence is sound. Section 4.5 T-A is not.

MUTATION: applied T-A verbatim in a scratch copy of apps/invoicing - the four 3.3 modules, exactly one SANCTIONED entry, literal 3->4; mutation asserted applied at both sites first. Baseline 13 tests/13 pass. After: 10 pass/3 fail. Predicted 1 red, observed 3, all classified:

D1 defect. "Gains exactly one SANCTIONED entry ... 3 -> 4" is wrong. The OUTBOUND_CLIENTS row 'stripe transport import' is /['"][^'"]*\btransport\.js['"]/ and matches lib/telemetry/client.js:2; SANCTIONED keys on file+construct+line, so the lib/stripe/client.js entry cannot absorb it. Two new entries -> 3 -> 5.

D2 defect. "The four new files are added to the SCANNED literal list" - no such list; SCANNED is a classifyTree filesystem walk. The real obligation is the count literal at test/dependency-policy.test.js:390, 63 -> 67.

D3 defect. test/dependency-policy.test.js is 1198 lines against the 1200-line cap its own test enforces. T-A's additions overflow it (observed 1208). Needs a decision the note does not make: split the file or raise the cap.

D4 defect. Section 4.2's type enum lists 15 of the 16 error classes in app source; WebhookEventError (routes/webhooks.js:30) is omitted, so it ships as the literal UnknownError on the Stripe webhook path. Fails safe, loses signal.

D5 defect, trivial. Section 3.2 attributes magic-string to @apm-js-collab/code-transformer; it is a dependency of the sibling @apm-js-collab/code-transformer-bundler-plugins@0.7.1. Real deps also include semifies.

D6 defect, minor. Section 4.3's "10" is produced by a hand-tuned regex and is a floor presented as a count: lib/contracts/generation.js:110 interpolates a deny-listed contract template variable and is not counted. Errs safe.

C1 convention, not a verdict. The plan is the task description verbatim - no numbered acceptance criteria, no M4 falsifiers; AC-1..AC-5 came from the tasking message. Routed to the record's owner.

CRITERIA SWEEP (floor check, M5): AC-1 five sections present, pass. AC-2 pass. AC-3 pass (T-C). AC-4 pass. AC-5 pass. 5 of 5, with 6 findings outside the list.

Worktree untouched (git status clean); all mutation confined to my scratchpad; no container started; no network used.

Cycle-1 rework committed: 7c56d4e on feat/AS-76-observability-design. All six findings fixed in the design note; nothing else touched.

D1 T-A: two SANCTIONED entries, literal 3 -> 5, with the mechanism spelled out (keys on file+construct+line; the 'stripe transport import' OUTBOUND_CLIENTS row matches ANY quoted transport.js). Construct string must stay 'stripe transport import' - it is matched against the row name, and the AS-38 recipes quote it; misnomer recorded in the entry reason.
D2: SCANNED is the classifyTree walk. Real obligation is the pair at dependency-policy.test.js:390-391 - 63 -> 67 plus the four paths sorted between lib/stripe/transport.js and lib/vendor.js.
D3 RULED - split, not a raised cap. The 1,200 is stack decision §10.4 item 1 / trigger T7 whose recorded remedy is 'Split it'; amending it as a side effect of a telemetry task is the wrong order. T-A step 0 moves stripComments/stripHashComments + their two self-tests + strippedText + SOURCE_EXT to test/helpers/source-text.js and test/source-text.test.js. MANIFEST_NAME stays (AS-53 M0 pins its line). AS-77 does it as its own commit before any telemetry code.
D4: WebhookEventError added - 16th of 16 measured classes; .reason/.step added to corollary 2.
D5: magic-string re-attributed to ...-bundler-plugins@0.7.1; semifies added. Re-ran Ruben's magic.js independently.
D6: 'floor 10, at least 11', naming lib/contracts/generation.js:110.

I then executed the rewritten T-A rather than asserting it: 17 tests/17 pass on a scratch copy, guard file 1,086 lines, then broken three ways. That run found two more defects in my own rewrite - F6's predicted red sets were wrong in both directions (both tests share scanForbidden), and the split also owes harness.test.js 23 -> 24. Both now in the note. Receipts: scratchpad/agent-cto-owen/AS-76/VERIFY-TA.md + apply-ta.js, f6-check.js, f6-check-b.js.

Ready for cycle-2 review.

VERDICT: PASS. Read cold (plan + diff only; did not read cycle-1's review or the implementer's comments). Receipts for every number: scratchpad/agent-qa-priya/AS-76/receipts.txt.

FINDINGS FIRST — 3 outside the criteria list, none violating a stated criterion, none blocking.

1. GUARD-HARDENING RESIDUAL, verified by observed red. Section 4.5's obligation set is complete for AS-77 but not for section 4.4's own ruling. I implemented 4.4 as written (HMAC-SHA-256 actor id + 32-byte install salt in lib/telemetry) and ran the guard: 'webhook signature HMAC: found in [lib/telemetry/actor.js, lib/webhooks/signature.js], allowed in exactly [lib/webhooks/signature.js]' and 'random bytes: found in [... lib/telemetry/actor.js], allowed in exactly [password.js, session.js]'. scanConcept's allowed list is an exact deepEqual, so both are hard reds. Section 4.5 step 3 says 'no new scanConcept row', the hazard list names only fetch and transport.js, and section 7's AS-78 paragraph orders the HMAC and salt with no guard note. Per the triage gate this folds into AS-78, not a new task. Note the 'webhook signature HMAC' row name becomes a misnomer exactly as 'stripe transport import' did.

2. PRECISION, section 2.3. 'server.js contains zero occurrences of any outbound-client construct' — the token fetch appears twice, apps/chat/server.js:1252 and :1257, both inside // comments. Zero under the guard's comment-stripping method, so the conclusion stands; the sentence is falsified by a plain grep and is flagged as measured.

3. NIT. Section 3.1 records Sentry's closure as 32 (floor); 3.2 and 3.4 say '33-package tree'. Both defensible under the >=33 caveat, two numbers for one quantity.

PROCESS OBSERVATION, not the author's: the plan file carries no numbered acceptance criteria and no '## Review Cycle 1 Findings' section. My criteria came from the tasking message.

CRITERIA SWEEP (floor check — 3 findings above sit outside it): AC-1 five sections a-e present, PASS. AC-2 section 6 is a verbatim ready-to-paste needs_human with no internal identifiers, PASS. AC-3 T-A/T-B/T-C named, T-C is the deny-list sweep, PASS. AC-4 SDK and raw ingest both argued and measured, PASS. AC-5 self-hosted vs cloud with ops burden and $0, PASS.

CYCLE-1 DEFECTS — all six re-verified independently, plus both secondaries. SANCTIONED 3->5 correct (the transport-import row is /['"][^'"]*\\btransport\\.js['"]/ at line 502, matches any scanned file). SCANNED is a walk; 63->67 plus the sorted array is the real obligation. 1198 vs the 1200 self-cap confirmed; split lands at 1086. 16 error classes measured, matching the enum exactly, WebhookEventError at routes/webhooks.js:30. magic-string re-attributed correctly (dep of code-transformer-bundler-plugins, not code-transformer). 185/60/10-floor-11-known all reproduce, generation.js:110 verbatim. harness 23->24 confirmed by running it red first. F6 run by me from the table, not their scripts: (a) 1 red outbound, (b) 2 reds outbound+sanction, (c) 2 reds outbound+sanction — exactly the table, green before and after restore.

PROBE PAST THE LIST: applied T-A end-to-end and ran the WHOLE suite, which the note's own verification did not. Failure census after is identical to baseline file for file (140 pre-existing host-side container-path failures both times), so four new lib/ files break no inventory beyond the three T-A names. Also re-derived 69/67/66 and the licence spread against stack decision amendment 8, the Sentry and PostHog closures, and every cited line anchor. No network was used at any point; no account, key or spend touched.

No inline fixes made; nothing committed to the branch.
